title: Beyond the Model: Harnessing Frontier AI for Stronger Cyber Defense
summary: When CrowdStrike tested frontier AI in vulnerability research, we learned the greatest differentiator wasn’t the model used, but the harness around it.
body_text: Frontier AI is fundamentally changing the pace of cybersecurity. For defenders and adversaries alike, it compresses the time required to discover vulnerabilities, assess exploitability, and act. AI models can reason across entire codebases, identify complex vulnerability chains, and generate exploit paths at a speed and scale that was previously impossible. That's a breakthrough for defenders, but it's also a preview of how quickly adversaries will evolve. At CrowdStrike, we wanted to answer a simple question: How do we turn frontier AI into better security outcomes? Over the past several months, we've been working with frontier AI models, including Anthropic's Mythos Preview, to understand how their capabilities perform in real-world vulnerability research and other security use cases. Along the way, we uncovered a series of lessons that extend well beyond vulnerability discovery, from how frontier AI should be operationalized to how it will reshape adversary tradecraft to what organizations must do to continuously strengthen cyber defense. This blog explores the first of those lessons: The model is only part of the equation. The real differentiator is how it's harnessed. Frontier AI Changes the Economics of Vulnerability Discovery Security leaders are facing a fundamental shift. The number of publicly disclosed vulnerabilities has dramatically increased over the past decade, and the pace continues to accelerate. By late June 2026, the number of published CVEs this year had already reached nearly two-thirds of the total reported during all of 2025 (Figure 1). Defenders aren't simply managing more vulnerabilities; they're managing an expanding attack surface that is growing faster every year. Figure 1. Growth in published CVEs from 2016 through 2026 (Data source: www.cvedetails.com) The window to respond is shrinking. The CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report found a 42% year-over-year increase in zero-day vulnerabilities exploited before public disclosure. Attackers are weaponizing vulnerabilities earlier in their lifecycle, giving defenders less time to identify, prioritize, and remediate risk before exploitation begins. Frontier AI will only accelerate this trend. When frontier AI models first demonstrated breakthrough performance on software engineering and reasoning tasks, we wanted to understand what those advances meant for cybersecurity. Could these models fundamentally change vulnerability research? Could they help security teams discover vulnerabilities faster, understand exploitability more accurately, and ultimately improve defensive outcomes? To answer those questions, we evaluated several frontier AI models, including Anthropic's Mythos Preview, across a range of real-world vulnerability discovery tasks. The results confirmed what many in the industry are already seeing: Frontier AI represents a significant advance in vulnerability research. These models can reason across large codebases, identify subtle relationships between vulnerabilities, and explore potential attack paths with a level of sophistication that was previously difficult to achieve at scale. Frontier AI models can reason across a wider aperture; as a result, they can recognize that what appears to be a low-severity information disclosure vulnerability becomes far more dangerous when combined with a memory corruption vulnerability and a privilege escalation path elsewhere in the application. It can evaluate whether existing mitigations can be bypassed, assess how an attacker might chain multiple weaknesses together, and produce a coherent attack narrative rather than a disconnected list of findings. This capability has profound implications for defenders. As AI accelerates vulnerability discovery, it will compress the time between discovery and exploitation. Organizations can no longer assume they have days or weeks to patch before attackers move. They must separate meaningful risk from overwhelming noise and translate AI-driven discovery into actionable security outcomes. On the flip side, the same advances give defenders an unprecedented opportunity to move faster, prioritize more effectively, and respond with greater confidence, provided they harness AI properly. The Harness Matters as Much as the Model Our testing exposed another important breakthrough: Finding vulnerabilities is only part of the challenge. Security teams need to know which findings represent real risk and which can safely be ignored. In our earliest tests, frontier AI models generated thousands of potential vulnerabilities. While many were legitimate, the majority proved to be theoretical, unreachable, or impossible to reproduce. The volume of findings quickly overwhelmed their value. So rather than asking which frontier model performed best, we began asking a different question: How do we operationalize frontier AI to gain a trusted view of vulnerability risk? As we continued our testing, one conclusion became increasingly clear: The frontier model wasn't the biggest differentiator. The way it was applied was. Rather than treating the model as a standalone capability, we built a security harness around it, combining structured threat modeling, exploit validation, workflow orchestration, and the deep security expertise embedded throughout the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform. Each stage serves a purpose. Threat modeling focused analysis on code that was reachable by an attacker. Validation reduced theoretical findings before they reached analysts. Exploit verification determined whether vulnerabilities could be chained together and reproduced in realistic environments. Together, these steps transformed raw AI output into actionable vulnerability intelligence. The results are profound. Using the same class of frontier AI models with different workflows produced dramatically different outcomes. A generic approach yielded false-positive rates approaching 80%. Applying CrowdStrike's security harness reduced that rate to approximately 20% while maintaining exceptional vulnerability discovery capability. More importantly, the improvement wasn't model-specific. It came from combining frontier AI with structured workflows, rigorous validation, and deep security expertise. As the pace of model innovation accelerates and organizations gain access to an expanding ecosystem of capable frontier models, the differentiator won’t necessarily be those with access to the newest and most powerful models. It will be the ability to operationalize AI to consistently deliver trusted security outcomes. This lesson applies equally to defenders and adversaries. Sophisticated threat actors won't simply adopt frontier AI; they'll engineer workflows around it to accelerate vulnerability discovery and exploitation. Defenders must do the same by applying AI in ways that improve speed and confidence rather than simply increasing volume. What We Found Leveraging Mythos Preview along with our proprietary harnesses optimized for vulnerability research, CrowdStrike analyzed nine categories of open-source software: network infrastructure, browsers, AI and developer tooling, virtualization platforms, search services, system software, databases, cryptographic libraries, and web sanitization tools. The findings are significant in both volume and severity. Across these categories, the pipeline surfaced more than 2,400 vulnerabilities. More than one in four findings (26%) were rated high or critical severity. Approximately 50% of confirmed findings carried working proof-of-concept exploits generated or validated by the pipeline. Table 1. Distribution of vulnerability findings by severity level Severity Vulnerabilities Percentage Critical 72 3% High 552 23% Medium 888 37% Low 744 31% Informational 144 6% The main takeaway is scale. In a matter of days, CrowdStrike’s AI-driven vulnerability research pipeline surfaced more than 2,400 vulnerability findings across 43 different products and nine major open-source software categories. Frontier AI, when paired with the right harness, can materially change the speed and scale of vulnerability discovery, helping defenders find and prioritize risk faster. A note on these findings: Results were generated through automated AI testing with human oversight, but not all have yet undergone full human triage with open-source maintainers and vendors. CrowdStrike is following responsible disclosure processes and will share additional details as this process is complete. Severity ratings, exploitability assessments, and proof-of-concept validity should be treated as informational at this stage. Three Lessons for Security Leaders Our testing reinforces three important lessons for security leaders preparing for the frontier AI era. 1. Evaluate AI by outcomes, not models The rapid pace of innovation in frontier AI means there will always be another model release, another benchmark, and another leaderboard. Those advances are only part of the equation. The real question isn't which model performs best in isolation; it's how effectively that model can be operationalized to solve real security problems. For defenders, success should be measured by outcomes: Can AI reduce false positives? Can it identify exploitable vulnerabilities with greater confidence? Can it integrate into existing security workflows and help teams make faster, more informed decisions? The organizations that realize the greatest value from frontier AI will be those that combine advanced models with security expertise, structured validation, and operational workflows that produce trusted, actionable results. 2. Prepare for AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery Defenders and adversaries alike will benefit from faster discovery and better analysis. As AI compresses the time between vulnerability discovery and exploitation, organizations can no longer assume they will have weeks, or even days, to remediate every critical vulnerability before attackers use them. Patching remains an essential security discipline, but it is no longer sufficient on its own. Security leaders should shift their focus from vulnerability management as a backlog exercise to continuous exposure management by understanding which assets are most critical, which vulnerabilities are most likely to be exploited, and where compensating controls can reduce risk while remediation is underway. 3. Build resilience, not just response Frontier AI is not a cyber superweapon. It is an accelerator. The organizations best prepared for the AI era will build environments that are resilient by design. This means assuming sophisticated adversaries will eventually gain an initial foothold and designing security architectures that limit what happens next. It means protecting identities as aggressively as endpoints, reducing unnecessary privileges, continuously validating exposure, monitoring for policy changes, governing AI systems, and automating detection and response across the attack surface. Most importantly, it means creating a continuous feedback loop where offensive research strengthens defensive capabilities. This enables organizations to adapt as quickly as the threat landscape evolves. Frontier AI represents one of the most significant advances in cybersecurity in decades. But the future of cybersecurity won't be defined by AI alone. The organizations that succeed will be the ones that combine frontier AI with deep security expertise, continuous validation, and a closed-loop approach that turns offensive discovery into stronger defense. That's the future CrowdStrike is building. Learn more The findings in this blog are a starting point. Here’s how to take action: Download our guide to explore the five steps for frontier AI security readiness. Visit our Frontier AI Readiness and Resilience Service page to learn about CrowdStrike’s approach to frontier AI and see how CrowdStrike Services can help. Learn how Falcon Exposure Management can help you discover, prioritize, and manage exposure risk across your environment. Check out our YouTube channel . Join us at Fal.Con 2026 as we bring together cyber leaders from across the industry to help secure the AI revolution.

title: ZIONS BANCORPORATION'S BOARD ANNOUNCES APPROVAL OF SHARE REPURCHASE AND DECLARES DIVIDENDS ON COMMON AND PREFERRED STOCK
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Zions Bancorporation, N.A. (NASDAQ: ZION) announced today that its board of directors has authorized share repurchases of up to $75 million of...
body_text: SALT LAKE CITY , July 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zions Bancorporation, N.A. (NASDAQ: ZION ) announced today that its board of directors has authorized share repurchases of up to $75 million of the company's common stock for the third quarter of 2026 as part of the company's previously authorized share repurchase target for 2026 of $300 million. The timing and amounts of any such actions will depend on market conditions, regulatory requirements, and other factors or uncertainties and may be updated at the discretion of the board. The board also declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.48 per common share, payable August 20, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on August 13, 2026. The dividend represents a $0.03, or 6.7%, increase from the prior quarter. Additionally, the board declared the regular quarterly cash dividend on the company's Series A perpetual preferred shares (NASDAQ: ZIONP ; CUSIP: 98973A104). The cash dividends on the preferred shares are payable September 15, 2026, to shareholders of record on September 1, 2026. Zions Bancorporation, N.A. is one of the nation's premier financial services companies with approximately $89 billion of total assets at December 31, 2025, and annual net revenue of $3.4 billion in 2025. Zions operates under local management teams and distinct brands in 11 western states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming. The Bank is a consistent recipient of national and state-wide customer survey awards in small- and middle-market banking, as well as a leader in public finance advisory services and Small Business Administration lending. In addition, Zions is included in the S&P MidCap 400 and NASDAQ Financial 100 indices. Investor information and links to local banking brands can be accessed at www.zionsbancorporation.com . SOURCE Zions Bancorporation

title: Classification UL 94 et matériaux plastiques ignifugés
summary: Analyse détaillée des thermoplastiques ignifugés et de la norme UL 94, avec critères, classifications et applications industrielles.
body_text: Lorsque vous concevez une pièce en plastique sans tenir compte des classements feu, vous prenez bien plus qu’un risque réglementaire. UL 94 n’est pas une simple mention technique : c’est souvent ce qui fait la différence entre un produit validé et une refonte coûteuse. La différence entre une classification V-0 et V-2 peut, à elle seule, déterminer l’approbation ou le rejet d’un projet en phase de certification. Si vous avez déjà vu une pièce pourtant parfaitement conçue échouer à un essai simplement parce que son épaisseur de paroi était inférieure au seuil requis, vous savez à quel point ces critères sont déterminants. Applications des plastiques ignifugés Les matériaux classés UL 94 sont couramment utilisés dans les applications suivantes : Composants automobiles sous capot (PA, PPS) Ventilateurs de refroidissement et supports (PBT, LCP) Boîtiers électriques et interrupteurs (PC, mélanges ABS/PC) Guides de câbles industriels et composants électroniques (PP, PEEK) Boîtiers de dispositifs médicaux (PPSU) Équipements télécoms et boîtiers de connecteurs (ABS, PC/ABS) Ces pièces sont souvent exposées à des températures élevées, à des charges mécaniques et à la proximité de courants électriques, ce qui rend la résistance au feu essentielle pour la sécurité et la conformité réglementaire. Qu’est-ce que la norme UL 94 ? Voyons concrètement ce qu’est la norme UL 94, pourquoi elle est souvent sous-estimée, et comment l’intégrer dès le départ pour faire des choix matériaux plus pertinents. UL 94 est une norme d’inflammabilité des plastiques développée par Underwriters Laboratories. Elle évalue la réaction des plastiques exposés à une flamme nue, en mesurant : le temps d’inflammation, la capacité d’auto-extinction, et la présence éventuelle de gouttes enflammées susceptibles d’allumer un indicateur en coton placé sous l’échantillon. La norme UL 94 est compatible avec d’autres standards internationaux, ce qui lui confère une portée mondiale en matière d’essais de sécurité incendie. Méthodes d’essai UL 94 Les configurations de test varient selon la classification : La classification HB repose sur un essai de combustion horizontale. Les classifications de la série V et 5V utilisent des éprouvettes ou plaques positionnées verticalement. Dans la série V, la différence entre V-0 et V-1 réside dans des critères plus exigeants appliqués dans des conditions de test identiques. Le passage de la série V à la série 5V implique des conditions d’essai nettement plus sévères, avec une exigence accrue en matière de résistance à la flamme. Classements UL 94 - aperçu synthétique Classement Critère principal HB Combustion lente sur une pièce horizontale V-2 Extinction en moins de 30 s sur une pièce verticale, avec gouttes enflammées autorisées V-1 Extinction en moins de 30 s sur une pièce verticale, gouttes non enflammées V-0 Extinction en moins de 10 s sur une pièce verticale, gouttes non enflammées 5VB Extinction en moins de 60 s sur une pièce verticale, sans gouttes enflammées ; percement possible 5VA Identique au 5VB, mais sans percement autorisé ; classification la plus élevée UL 94 Conditions d’essai détaillées La classification 5VA / 5VB repose sur un essai de combustion verticale sur 125 mm à l’aide d’une flamme de brûleur Bunsen. Les éprouvettes (barres ou plaques) doivent respecter des dimensions et épaisseurs spécifiques. La flamme est appliquée par cycles de cinq secondes, avec cinq secondes sans flamme entre chaque application. Pour la série V, une flamme de 20 mm est appliquée deux fois pendant dix secondes. La seconde application intervient une fois l’échantillon éteint, ou immédiatement s’il ne s’enflamme pas. Configurations d’essai UL 94 Essai de combustion horizontale Essai de combustion verticale 20 mm Essai de combustion verticale 125 mm (barre) Essai de combustion verticale 125 mm (plaque) Matériaux ignifugés vs matériaux résistants à la flamme Les matériaux ignifugés sont formulés pour ralentir l’inflammation et limiter la propagation de la flamme. Ils peuvent s’enflammer, mais s’auto-éteignent lorsque la source d’ignition est retirée. Les classifications UL 94 entrent dans cette catégorie. Les matériaux résistants à la flamme, en revanche, sont conçus pour empêcher l’inflammation. Ils sont généralement utilisés dans les textiles ou les équipements de protection individuelle et sont évalués selon d’autres normes, comme ASTM D6413 ou ISO 15025. Comprendre cette distinction permet de choisir un matériau adapté à la fois aux exigences fonctionnelles et au cadre réglementaire. Pourquoi l’épaisseur et la formulation sont déterminantes Les classifications UL 94 dépendent de l’épaisseur. Une résine validée à 1,5 mm peut échouer à 0,74 mm. Certains matériaux offrent une performance stable sur une large plage d’épaisseurs, mais ce n’est jamais garanti. La formulation joue également un rôle clé. La plupart des grades ignifugés reposent sur des additifs spécifiques. De légères modifications, comme un changement de colorant, peuvent invalider une certification si la nouvelle formulation n’est pas testée et certifiée séparément. En cas de doute, demandez toujours une UL Yellow Card à votre fournisseur de matière. Ce document atteste que le matériau a été testé et certifié, pour une formulation donnée et sur une plage d’épaisseurs définie. Matériaux ignifugés disponibles chez Protolabs Protolabs propose une large sélection de matériaux classés UL 94 pour le moulage par injection et l’impression 3D . Des résines fournies par le client peuvent également être évaluées sur demande. Attention : un même matériau peut présenter des classements différents selon l’épaisseur, la formulation ou le procédé. Il ne suffit donc pas de dire qu’un matériau est « V-0 ». En complément des nombreux matériaux ignifugés disponibles en moulage par injection, deux matériaux ignifugés sont proposés en impression 3D : ESD Black (Loctite 3380) Résine classée UL 94 V-0 à 2,0 mm. Elle offre des propriétés dissipatives ESD et convient aux pièces imprimées nécessitant une grande précision et un haut niveau de détail. Arkema FR512 Photopolymère ignifugé utilisé dans le procédé HPS, classé UL 94 V-0 à 0,79 mm. Idéal pour les pièces complexes nécessitant une résolution fine et une certification feu. En savoir plus sur les matériaux ignifugés pour l’impression 3D Les PFAS dans les matériaux ignifuges Les substances per- et polyfluoroalkylées (PFAS) sont utilisées depuis longtemps dans les additifs ignifuges en raison de leur résistance thermique et chimique exceptionnelle. Cependant, les PFAS font aujourd’hui l’objet d’une pression réglementaire croissante en raison de leur persistance dans l’environnement et de leurs liens avec des risques potentiels pour la santé. Si certains matériaux ignifuges contiennent encore des PFAS, de nombreux fabricants s’en détournent. Nous suivons de près la réglementation relative aux PFAS. Bien que la teneur en PFAS ne figure pas actuellement dans nos fiches techniques, nous encourageons les clients ayant des préoccupations d'ordre réglementaire ou environnemental à nous contacter. Nous pouvons vous aider à explorer des alternatives ou à confirmer la composition spécifique des résines si nécessaire. Considérations environnementales Les retardateurs de flamme améliorent la sécurité incendie, mais peuvent compliquer la gestion de la fin de vie des produits. Les additifs halogénés sont difficiles à séparer lors du recyclage et peuvent libérer des composés toxiques en cas d'incinération. C'est pourquoi on s'intéresse de plus en plus aux retardateurs de flamme non halogénés, qui offrent des performances similaires tout en réduisant l'empreinte environnementale. Le choix des matériaux doit toujours tenir compte à la fois de la sécurité et de la durabilité. Pourquoi les indices de résistance au feu sont-ils importants dans le développement de produits ? Les indices UL 94 ne sont pas de simples détails techniques. Ils déterminent souvent si une pièce peut être utilisée dans des secteurs réglementés tels que l'aérospatiale, le médical, l'automobile et l'électronique grand public. Choisir dès le début un matériau certifié pour sa résistance au feu permet d'éviter les problèmes de conformité, les modifications de conception coûteuses et les échecs de certification en fin de cycle. Une dernière chose avant de soumettre votre conception La certification UL est spécifique à chaque formulation. Une résine peut être certifiée « Yellow Card », mais les mélanges sur mesure, les colorants, les additifs et toute autre modification apportée au matériau de base peuvent affecter son classement. Si vous travaillez dans des secteurs où s’appliquent plusieurs normes relatives aux propriétés, telles que celles concernant la fumée, la toxicité ou le vieillissement thermique, veillez à valider l’ensemble du profil du matériau avant la production. Pour plus d'informations sur les propriétés des matériaux de moulage par injection, consultez notre Guide de sélection des matériaux de moulage par injection . La norme UL 94 peut sembler être une simple clause réglementaire, mais elle joue un rôle déterminant dans ce qui est fabriqué, ce qui est approuvé et ce qui doit être repensé. Nos ingénieurs d'application sont à votre disposition pour vous aider à prendre la bonne décision en fonction de votre application, de votre budget et de votre calendrier. Demander un devis Prêt à choisir un matériau certifié UL 94 et à éviter des modifications de conception coûteuses ? Téléchargez votre pièce pour obtenir immédiatement un devis et connaître les délais de livraison. Foire aux questions Qu'est-ce que la norme UL 94 et pourquoi est-elle importante ? expand_less expand_more La norme UL 94 est une norme d'inflammabilité des plastiques établie par Underwriters Laboratories qui évalue la réaction des matériaux face à une flamme nue, leur inflammabilité, leur capacité d'auto-extinction, ainsi que la capacité des gouttes enflammées à enflammer un indicateur en coton. Largement reconnue et souvent exigée dans les secteurs réglementés, la classification que vous choisissez peut déterminer si une pièce obtient la certification ou doit être repensée. Que signifient les principales classifications UL 94 (HB, V et 5V) ? expand_less expand_more HB : Combustion lente sur un échantillon horizontal. V-2 : L'échantillon vertical cesse de brûler en moins de 30 s ; les gouttes enflammées susceptibles d'enflammer le coton sont autorisées. V-1 : L'échantillon vertical cesse de brûler en moins de 30 s ; aucune goutte enflammée susceptible d'enflammer le coton. V-0 : L'échantillon vertical cesse de brûler en moins de 10 s ; aucune goutte enflammée susceptible d'enflammer le coton. 5VB/5VA : Essais verticaux plus rigoureux utilisant une flamme plus importante ; aucune goutte enflammée n'est autorisée. La norme 5VB autorise la combustion traversante (trous), contrairement à la norme 5VA, qui est la classification UL 94 la plus élevée. Dans quelle mesure l'épaisseur et la composition d'une pièce influent-elles sur la classification UL 94 ? expand_less expand_more Les classifications dépendent de l'épaisseur et sont spécifiques à chaque formulation. Une résine classée V-0 à 1,5 mm peut ne pas satisfaire aux exigences à 0,8 mm, et même de légères modifications de la formulation (comme l'ajout d'un nouveau colorant) peuvent invalider une classification antérieure. Vérifiez toujours la fiche technique UL (UL Yellow Card) du matériau et assurez-vous qu'elle couvre précisément votre formulation et votre plage d'épaisseurs. Quelle est la différence entre les matériaux ignifugés et les matériaux résistants au feu ? expand_less expand_more Les matériaux ignifuges sont conçus pour retarder l'inflammation et s'éteindre d'eux-mêmes dès que la source de flamme est supprimée (la norme UL 94 s'applique ici). Les matériaux résistants au feu sont conçus pour empêcher toute inflammation et sont testés selon d'autres normes (par exemple, ASTM D6413, ISO 15025), couramment utilisées pour les textiles et les EPI. Quels sont les matériaux ignifuges proposés par Protolabs, et qu'en est-il des PFAS et des préoccupations environnementales ? expand_less expand_more Protolabs propose de nombreuses résines certifiées UL 94 pour le moulage par injection, ainsi que certaines options ignifuges pour l'impression 3D. Exemple : la résine Arkema FR512 (photopolymère) obtient la certification UL 94 V-0 à une épaisseur de 0,031 pouce (0,79 mm). Les résines fournies par le client peuvent être évaluées sur demande. Notez que les classifications varient selon la qualité et l'épaisseur ; ne présumez pas d'une classification « V-0 » générale. Certains systèmes ignifuges peuvent contenir des PFAS ou des additifs halogénés ; nous suivons de près la réglementation et pouvons vous aider à confirmer la composition de la résine ou à explorer des alternatives non halogénées afin de soutenir la recyclabilité et les objectifs environnementaux.

title: Consejos para conducir en ciudad mientras llueve
summary: Sigue estos sencillos consejos para conducir bajo la lluvia y evitar accidentes, recuerda que es mejor prevenir.
body_text: Conducir bajo la lluvia es muy diferente a hacerlo en condiciones normales, pues el pavimento mojado y la lluvia dificultan la visibilidad y la estabilidad del auto. Esto es especialmente relevante al manejar en la ciudad , pues existe una gran cantidad de autos en el tránsito y los constantes semáforos pueden aumentar el riesgo de sufrir un accidente. Por estas razones, compartimos contigo algunos consejos que te pueden ayudar a evitarlos. Prende las luces. Los primero para conducir en la lluvia es mantener tu visibilidad del camino . Por eso que debes encender las luces delanteras, no importa si es de día o de noche. La luz también ayudará a que seas más visible para los demás conductores. Si la lluvia es muy intensa y tu auto cuenta con ellas, prende los faros de niebla delanteros y traseros. Utiliza las intermitentes. En el mismo orden de ser visible para los demás conductores e incluso para los peatones, será necesario usar las luces intermitentes. Para avisar que te vas a detener, tal vez no sea suficiente las luces traseras, es una muy buena idea prender las intermitentes de tu auto cuando vas a frenar y después apagarlas cuando reinicies tu marcha. Este consejo es de especial atención al manejar durante tormentas pues es fácil no ver el alto delante tuyo y deberás frenar rápidamente. Debes estar seguro que el auto detrás tuyo se entere lo más pronto posible que frenarás. Utilizar el aire acondicionado Para mantener una correcta visibilidad es importante evitar el paño en los vidrios del auto. Una de las formas para desempañar la luna del auto y los demás vidrios, es utilizando el aire acondicionado. Este sistema junto con la calefacción ayudan a desempañar los vidrios del auto. Aunque se debe mencionar que el aire calientes es mejor para solucionar este problema. Utilizar repelente de agua Hasta ahora hemos solucionado el paño en los vidrios del auto, pero cuando la lluvia es demasiado intensa, el agua del exterior puede dificultar la visión. Para evitar que en las ventanillas laterales de tu auto se acumulen las gotas de lluvia, usa repelente de agua. Esto no permitirá que el líquido se adhiera al vidrio y obstruya tu visión. Así que en temporada de lluvias será mejor aplicar repelente a los vidrios de tu auto y en especial al parabrisas. Te puede interesar: 7 sencillas forma de cuidar el parabrisas de tu auto En este sentido también debemos contar con limpiaparabrisas en buen estado para que nos ayuden a mantener el parabrisas libre de agua en caso de lluvia. Evita la brisa de otros autos Al conducir con precipitaciones es normal casi todos los autos producen una brisa que impacta el auto detrás de ellos. Este problema se agrava cuando se trata de vehículos grandes. Muchos camiones producen una brisa extra capaz de llegar a impregnar el parabrisas de tu auto y dificultan aún más tu visibilidad. Si te es posible, revásalos, de lo contrario aumenta tu distancia para evitar que la brisa llegue a tu parabrisas. Mantener la estabilidad del auto El segundo problema más grave al manejar con lluvia es mantener el auto estable. Debido a la lluvia es muy frecuente que las llantas pierdan tracción con el pavimento , incluso se produce el hidroplaneo. En la cubierta de los neumáticos de tu auto existen pequeños canales que permiten el paso del agua para evitar que se interponga entre el neumático y el asfalto. En chubascos poco intensos, el agua en el pavimento es desalojada por estos canales y el neumático se adhiere firmemente al pavimento. Sin embargo, cuando la lluvia es muy intensa, hay demasiada agua y estos canales no pueden desalojarla, provocando el hidroplaneo , también llamado “deslizamiento” o “patinar”. ¿Cómo salir de un deslizamiento? Para salir de un deslizamiento y tener de nueva cuenta el control del auto, toma nota: Mantén la calma, por muy difícil que sea. Deja de acelerar. Retira despacio el pie del acelerador. Mantén el volante firme y no trates de virar para ningún lado. El auto perderá velocidad y volverá a tener contacto con el asfalto y podrás retomar el control. Revisa tus neumáticos Continuando con el punto anterior es relevante mencionar que debes de mantener las llantas de tu auto en las mejores condiciones para mejorar tu seguridad al conducir bajo la lluvia. Los neumáticos de tu auto no deben estar demasiados desgastados o "lisos" como se le llega a conocer. Un truco muy sencillo para saber si debes cambiar tus llantas es introducir una moneda de un peso en los surcos del neumático. Si logras ver la circunferencia plateada, es momento de cambiarlas. Te puede interesar: 10 consejos para cuidar las llantas de tu auto Frena por pausas Como ya se mencionó anteriormente, con la lluvia los neumáticos pierden tracción con el asfalto. Por eso, al frenar y dentro de lo posible, evita hacerlo de forma abrupta pues en estas condiciones puedes tardar más en detenerte por completo. Por eso, anticipa los altos y frena en pausas. No podemos dejar de mencionar un consejo de expertos conductores para secar los frenos de tu auto. En estas condiciones de humedad los frenos de tu auto pueden perder agarre con el disco del eje del auto. Una forma para quitar ese exceso de humedad es frenar en varias ocasiones, te explicamos: cuando no tengas muy cerca otro auto, pisa el freno ligeramente más fuerte a lo usual en varias ocasiones. Este roce del freno con el disco quitará el agua extra en los frenos. Esta acción se debe realizar con precaución y cuando no tengas un auto muy cerca a ti para evitar accidentes. Aumenta tu distancia y baja la velocidad Un tercer punto esencial para conducir con lluvia es aumentar tu distancia con los otros autos. Aumenta la distancia que tienes con el auto delantero para que, en caso de ser necesario, te sea posible frenar a tiempo . Si vas por encima de los 40 km/h, deja un espacio por lo menos de 7 metros entre el auto delantero y el tuyo. Además, debes de reducir tu velocidad. La regla señala que conduzcas a la mitad de la velocidad permitida en la avenida cuando esté lloviendo. Mantenimiento del auto Además de los neumáticos, cuando inicie la temporada de lluvias debes considerar revisar los siguientes puntos a tu auto: Presión de los neumáticos Alineación y balanceo Cambio de aceite Sistema de frenos Luces y limpiaparabrisas Carga de la batería. Te puede interesar: Tipos de luces en tu auto y cómo utilizarlas Evita los estancamientos de agua No conduzcas sobre acumulamientos de agua y menos si vas a gran velocidad, ya que podrías perder el control del auto o encontrarte un bache. Es preferible que cambies de carril para evitarlo o si no tienes alternativa disminuyas considerablemente tu velocidad. No cruces corrientes de agua Cuando se producen grandes tormentas es común encontrar avenidas con una gran corriente de agua. Si este es el caso procura evitarlas y encuentra otro camino. Si no tienes alternativa, m antén el pie en el acelerador y no cambies de dirección de forma brusca. Cuidar a los peatones En la lluvia es común encontrar a personas corriendo para protegerse de la lluvia, es por eso que debes estar más al pendiente de las personas y darles la preferencia del paso. Mantén la calma Por último, es importante que tomes en cuenta que debido a la lluvia el tránsito irá más lento, debes ser más paciente y conservar la calma. Orillarte es una opción A pesar de todos los consejos anteriores, siempre será complicado conducir con lluvia. Si te sientes demasiado desconfiado en manejar en estas condiciones, es mejor que te orilles y esperes que la lluvia pare o por lo menos disminuya su intensidad. Puedes encontrar un estacionamiento alto en un centro comercial , o una calle poco transitada, sólo importan evitar zonas profundas que podrían llegar a inundarse. Te puede interesar: ¿Cómo pasar una calle inundada sin quedarte varado? Estos son varios consejos al conducir bajo la lluvia. title: How Greif Uses ESG Ratings to Drive Transparency, Accountability and Continuous Improvement
summary: At Greif, we believe transparency is essential to building trust with customers, suppliers, investors and other stakeholders. That’s why we monitor and
body_text: At Greif, we believe transparency is essential to building trust with customers, suppliers, investors and other stakeholders. That’s why we monitor and advance our performance across leading Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) assessments, including EcoVadis, Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI), Sustainalytics, Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and the S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA), which independently evaluate our environmental, social and governance performance. These ratings help customers assess supplier risk, make informed sourcing decisions and understand how Greif manages sustainability-related opportunities and challenges. Information from these assessments are provided to asset managers to support their understanding of sustainability-related risk and opportunity management, transparency, and comparison across peer companies. We use the results to drive continuous improvement in our sustainable business practices, data transparency and reporting, and identifying best practices. Here’s a closer look at the ratings, our results and their impact across our value chain. EcoVadis: Delivering Value Beyond Sustainability EcoVadis remains a strategic priority for many organizations because it is one of the most widely used sustainability assessments in global supply chains and is increasingly leveraged by customers during supplier selection and evaluation processes. The assessment measures performance across environmental, labor and human rights, ethics and sustainable procurement topics, assigning a score from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating stronger sustainability performance. In 2022, Greif signed a sustainable financing agreement to tie our loan pricing to routinely updated EcoVadis scores. Our 2026 renewal extends this agreement thought 2031. Greif’s commitment to continuous improvement is reflected in our EcoVadis performance. From 2023 to 2026, we increased our score by more than 13%, rising from 69 to 78, while consistently ranking in the 90th percentile or higher among assessed companies. Greif’s improved score of 74 in 2025 generated approximately $239,000 in savings in 2026. Building on this progress, the increase to 78 in 2026 is expected to deliver an additional $0.2 million in annual savings from March 2027 through March 2031. Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI): Measuring Resilience to Sustainability Risks MSCI ESG Ratings assess how effectively companies manage the topics MSCI considers to present financially relevant sustainability risks and opportunities, assigning ratings from AAA (Leader) to CCC (Laggard). Greif has maintained an A rating or higher since 2021, reflecting our ongoing commitment to environmental stewardship, transparency, and responsible business practices. Sustainalytics: Demonstrating Lower ESG Risk Morningstar Sustainalytics ESG Risk Ratings evaluate both a company’s exposure to sustainability-related risks and its ability to manage them. Scores range from 0 to 40+, with lower scores indicating lower unmanaged risk. Greif has consistently earned a Low Risk rating, improving its score from 19.0 in 2024 to 15.8 in 2026. These ratings help Greif better understand and manage sustainability-related risks while providing customers, suppliers and investors with an independent view of our long-term resilience and operational stability. Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS): Advancing Transparency Through Disclosure Greif is evaluated by ISS through its Environmental & Social (E&S) Disclosure QualityScore, which assesses the quality and completeness of corporate sustainability disclosures relative to industry peers. Scores range from 1 to 10, with 1 representing the strongest performance. ISS incorporates these scores into its annual proxy voting recommendations and communications with asset managers. Throughout 2024 and 2025, Greif’s Environmental and Social scores consistently ranged between 2 and 3, demonstrating strong disclosure and management practices across key ESG topics. Greif also received an ISS ESG Corporate Rating of B-, positioning the Company among the industry leaders in ESG performance and management. These assessments provide valuable insight into our sustainability reporting and help reinforce stakeholder confidence in the quality, transparency and consistency of our disclosures. S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment: A Broader ESG Perspective Greif also participates in the S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA), one of the world’s most recognized sustainability benchmarking frameworks. The assessment evaluates a company’s performance across a wide range of environmental, social and governance topics and serves as the foundation for several prominent sustainability indices and evaluations. Participation in the CSA allows Greif to benchmark its performance against global industry peers while gaining additional insight into opportunities for improvement. The assessment complements other ESG ratings by providing a broader view of sustainability management practices and organizational maturity. Why These Ratings Matter Each ESG rating provides a different perspective on sustainability performance, but together they offer stakeholders a more complete view of how partners like Greif manage ESG risks and opportunities. These independent assessments help validate our sustainability commitments, strengthen transparency, support customer supplier qualification processes and benchmark our performance against industry peers. Most importantly, they give customers, suppliers and business partners confidence that Greif is committed to responsible business practices, continuous improvement and creating long-term value across the supply chain. Greif continues to advance its sustainability journey through participation in leading ESG assessments, including EcoVadis, MSCI, Sustainalytics, ISS, and the S&P CSA. Learn more about our progress and commitments in our Informe de sostenibilidad . For questions, please contact Sustainability@greif.com .

title: Vicor Corporation Reports Results for the Second Quarter Ended June 30, 2026
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Vicor Corporation's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version ANDOVER, Mass., July 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vicor Corporation (NASDAQ: VICR) today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. These results will be discussed at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time, during management’s quarterly investor conference call. The details for the call are below. Product and royalty revenues for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 totaled $143.4 million, a 26.9% sequential increase from $113.0 million in the first quarter of 2026, compared to $141.0 million from product revenues, royalty revenues and a patent litigation settlement of $45.0 million for the corresponding period a year ago. Gross margin increased sequentially to $83.1 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $62.4 million for the first quarter of 2026, and decreased from $92.1 million for the corresponding period a year ago. Gross margin, as a percentage of revenue, increased to 58.0% for the second quarter of 2026, compared to 55.2% for the first quarter of 2026. Gross margin decreased from 65.3% for the corresponding period a year ago which included the aforementioned $45.0 million patent litigation settlement. Operating expenses increased sequentially to $48.2 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $45.5 million for the first quarter of 2026, and increased from $46.7 million for the corresponding period a year ago. Net income for the second quarter was $49.8 million, or $1.04 per diluted share, compared to net income of $20.7 million, or $0.44 per diluted share, for the first quarter of 2026 and net income of $41.2 million or $0.91 per diluted share, for the corresponding period a year ago. Cash flow from operations totaled $34.0 million for the second quarter, compared to cash flow used for operations of $(3.9) million in the first quarter of 2026, which included the impact of a $28.6 million payment of an award for past litigation, and cash flow from operations of $65.2 million for the corresponding period a year ago. Capital expenditures for the second quarter totaled $11.2 million, compared to $12.4 million for the first quarter of 2026 and $6.2 million for the corresponding period a year ago. Cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026 increased 12.2% sequentially to approximately $453.6 million compared to approximately $404.2 million as of March 31, 2026. Backlog for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 totaled $380 million, a 26% sequential increase from $301 million at the end of the first quarter of 2026, and increased 145% from $155 million for the corresponding period a year ago. Commenting on second quarter performance, Chief Executive Officer Dr. Patrizio Vinciarelli stated: “Rising demand across high-performance compute, automatic test equipment, and industrial, aerospace and defense applications is absorbing increased capacity within our first ChiP fab. As we get closer to full capacity utilization, we are taking steps toward a second fab for high current density 2nd Gen VPD ChiPs. AI OEMs and Hyper-scalers are at a loss dealing with the current density and PDN limitations of 1st Gen. VPD systems. The industry’s fixation with PoL regulators (replacing VRs, operating from 12V or 6V, with IVRs, operating from 1.8V) merely trades off one handicap (low current density) for another (low current gain). Feeding IVRs with a current multiplier is an incremental opportunity for Vicor. With its 2nd Gen VPD IP, Vicor is uniquely equipped to overcome the power system challenges standing in the way of future advances in TPUs, GPUs and Wafer Scale Engines.” For more information on Vicor and its products, please visit the Company’s website at www.vicorpower.com . Earnings Conference Call Vicor will be holding its investor conference call today, Tuesday, July 21, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Vicor encourages investors and analysts who intend to ask questions via the conference call to register with Notified, the service provider hosting the conference call. Those registering on Notified’s website will receive dial-in info and a unique PIN to join the call as well as an email confirmation with the details. Registration may be completed at any time prior to 8:00 a.m. on July 21, 2026. For those parties interested in listen-only mode, the conference call will be webcast via a link that will be posted on the Investor Relations page of Vicor's website prior to the conference call. Please access the website at least 15 minutes prior to the conference call to register and, if necessary, download and install any required software. For those who cannot participate in the live conference call, a webcast replay of the conference call will also be available on the Investor Relations page of Vicor's website. title: AI Agents Amplify Your Data Problems at Scale | Elementary Data
summary: Don't set AI up to fail. 57% of enterprises deployed AI agents in 2025, but data quality issues block 42%. Learn why fixing data foundations before scaling AI isn't slowing down—it's setting up to succeed.
body_text: We are no longer in the POCs phase, 2026 is the year of AI in production. According to Anthropic's recent research , 57% of enterprises deployed AI agents to production in 2025. Another 81% plan to tackle more complex use cases in 2026. And when you look at where organizations are seeing the highest impact, data analysis tops the list at 60%, followed by process automation at 48%. This makes sense, AI agents excel at synthesizing information, identifying patterns, and executing workflows that would take humans hours or days. Additionally, data analysis is a fundamental building block. Think about agents that need to make decisions in the organization, operate on their own and perform tasks. Same as humans, they need data and insights to act. High quality AI data analysis will power a endless valuable agentic workflows. The potential is clear.But here's the question too few organizations are asking: What happens when AI agents inherit your data problems? Because they will inherit them. Every single one. AI Is New. The Problems Aren't. If you've worked in data for any length of time, you've heard the same challenges described under different names: data fragmentation, low data adoption, or my favorite so far - “the analytics graveyard”. Organizations invest heavily in data infrastructure, warehouses, pipelines, transformation layers, BI tools, but struggle to get ROI from that investment. The root causes are familiar: Low trust. People don't believe the data is accurate. They've been burned before by reports that didn't match reality, so they build their own spreadsheets, run their own queries, double-check everything manually. Poor discovery. The data exists somewhere, but people can't find it. Tribal knowledge determines who knows what's available. New team members spend weeks figuring out which tables to use. Silos. Different teams have different "truths." Marketing's revenue number doesn't match Finance's. The data warehouse has three customer tables, and nobody remembers why. Persona gaps. The data platform was built by engineers, for engineers. Business users can't access what they need without filing a ticket and waiting. These problems have persisted for years. Organizations learned to work around them. Analysts developed intuition about which data to trust. Stakeholders accepted that getting answers takes time. Data teams became skilled at navigating the mess. But here's the critical point for your AI strategy: Humans can work around the mess. AI agents can't. When an analyst encounters a suspicious number, they pause. They investigate. They ask a colleague, "Does this look right to you?" They apply judgment born from experience. AI agents don't do that. They take the data at face value and act on it. Fast, and at scale. What Changes with AI The problems aren't new. But AI fundamentally changes their impact. Consider the amplification: Bad data used to mean a wrong report. A dashboard showed incorrect numbers. Someone caught it in a meeting. The data team fixed it. Embarrassing, but contained. Bad data now means hundreds of wrong AI decisions. An agent automating customer communications sends messages based on stale data. An agent managing inventory reorders products based on corrupted demand signals. An agent pricing deals uses metrics that haven't been updated.Each decision compounds. Each error propagates. Discovery gaps used to mean slow answers. A business user had a question. It took him time to find the right dataset, or he was dependent on getting an answer from the data team. Frustrating, but manageable. Discovery gaps now mean hallucinating agents. When an AI agent can't find the authoritative data source, it doesn't wait patiently for help. It makes something up. It infers. It confidently presents fabricated answers as fact. Or it uses the wrong table entirely, one that's been deprecated for months but still exists in the warehouse. Governance holes used to mean compliance risk. Somewhere in your data platform, PII exists in places it shouldn't. Access controls are inconsistent. A future audit might flag it. A problem for later. Governance holes now mean automated privacy violations. An AI agent, given broad data access to do its job, inadvertently incorporates sensitive information into its outputs. It shares customer data it shouldn't have access to. It distributes protected information. At scale. Automatically. With no human reviewing each action. The formula is simple: same problems, but at scale, machine speed, and higher stakes. AI doesn't create new data problems. But it dramatically amplifies the ones you already have. The Evidence Is Already Clear This isn't theoretical. Anthropic's research on enterprise AI adoption reveals that the top barriers organizations face are exactly what you'd expect: Data integration challenges: 46% Data quality issues: 42% Data problems as primary obstacle. Not model capabilities. Not compute costs. Not talent gaps. The ability to bring together information from across the organization into a coherent reliable whole that AI agents can use. These numbers tell a story: organizations are racing to deploy AI agents, then hitting walls their data infrastructure wasn't built to handle. The shift from the analytics era to the AI era isn't just about new technology. It's about new consumers of your data. In the analytics era, data flowed to humans: analysts, executives, business users. Humans could interpret, question, and compensate for imperfections. In the AI era, data flows to agents: systems that will consume it literally, act on it immediately, and scale its implications exponentially. The chief of software at Vercel put it bluntly: "If your data layer is a mess of legacy naming conventions and undocumented joins, giving Claude raw file access won't save you. You'll just get faster bad queries." Faster bad queries. Faster bad decisions. Faster bad outcomes. That's the amplification effect. The Responsible Path Forward Let me be direct: deploying AI agents without strong data foundations is irresponsible. This isn't about being conservative or slow. Organizations should absolutely pursue AI. The competitive advantages are too significant to ignore. But pursuing AI means taking data foundations seriously in a way that "nice to have" dashboards never demanded. What does "strong data foundations" actually mean? At minimum: Availability. Your data is consolidated, discoverable, and accessible to the systems that need it. AI agents can't work across fragmented silos any more than humans can, they just fail faster. Quality. Freshness is monitored. Issues are detected and resolved quickly. The agents get live visibility into data health, not just data existence. Governance. Access controls are defined and enforced programmatically. Sensitive data is classified and protected. There are audit trails for what data was used, when, and by whom. Modeling for AI. Naming conventions are clear. Relationships between entities are documented. Business terms have definitions that agents can understand. Your semantic layer, whether that's dbt models, a metrics layer, or well-documented tables, is rich enough that an AI can navigate it. This isn't an exhaustive list, and getting there isn't a weekend project. But the organizations succeeding with AI agents share a common trait: they invested in these foundations before scaling AI, not after. Not Slowing Down. Setting Up to Succeed. The message here isn't "pump the brakes on AI." The message is "don't set AI up to fail." The enterprises that will win with AI agents aren't necessarily the ones that deploy fastest. They're the ones whose agents produce reliable results. Whose automated decisions can be trusted. Whose AI-powered workflows actually deliver the promised value instead of creating new categories of problems. Those enterprises will have addressed their data foundations. Not perfectly, but sufficiently. They'll have moved from tolerating data problems to resolving them. From working around the mess to cleaning it up. Because AI agents amplify everything. The data ROI and the data problems.The question is: what do you want amplified? This is the first post in a series on data foundations for AI. Next: what "AI readiness" actually means, a practical framework for preparing your data for autonomous agents.

title: Getting More Out of Every AI Token
summary: As a software engineer, together with my colleagues at monday.com and also other engineers in the industry, I bore witness ...
body_text: As a software engineer, together with my colleagues at monday.com and also other engineers in the industry, I bore witness to some amazing changes in the world around us and our craft. First, the industry was bewitched by the possibilities that AI-driven development offered. We started to use AI a lot, learning as we go how to actually do this effectively. And we spent a lot. According to a Research and Markets report , the AI code tools market was worth $9.46 billion in 2026. If that number is a little too abstract, it could buy us around 1.5 billion Big Macs in California. When the bill came, executives around the globe, Monday included, realized that while AI is mighty, it’s also very much not free. Suddenly, the honeymoon period was over, and we needed to quickly learn how to not only be productive but also cost-effective. But it was never about money alone – nobody wants to work while worrying about hitting a spending limit. Fortunately, there are plenty of strategies we can adopt to improve cost efficiency and put these worries to bed. In this article, we will focus on the boundaries between the model and the user and between the model and the tools. In other words, we will teach our agents to use fewer words and mean more. Short anatomy of LLM costs LLMs are very talkative by nature. They love the fluff and flattery, and they write each response about a technical problem like they would write a recipe for a cake on a cooking blog. While reading about what a great and observant engineer I am is nice, it also doesn’t really contribute to solving my problem, unless my problem is imposter syndrome. Also, it takes time to read, and it uses expensive output tokens to produce it. Anthropic’s Opus 4.8, one of the most capable models at the time of writing, costs $5 per million input tokens and five times more – $25 per million output tokens (nearly four Big Macs, if we are not on keto). Cut the chatter: trim model replies with Caveman That’s why the Caveman plugin was created, to instruct our agents to be more terse and cut out the chit-chat. We could be asking: My Express auth middleware is letting expired JWT tokens through. The expiry check uses Date.now() compared to the token's exp field. What's wrong, and how do I fix it? And a non-caveman agent would start: Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is most likely caused by your authentication middleware not properly validating the token expiry. Let me take a look and suggest a fix [...] That’s 40 tokens already, and we haven’t even started on the real answer. I don’t want to hear about pleasantries and words of encouragement. I want a caveman: Bug: `exp` is seconds, `Date.now()` is milliseconds. Comparing raw = expired tokens pass. Fix: compare `Date.now() / 1000 > exp` (or `exp * 1000`). On average, according to its own benchmarks, Caveman cuts 65% of output tokens. Mind that it’s not only about the financial cost of a token, but also about the human cost of reading the output. This output will also stay in the context and will be sent on each conversation turn. It will be cached, and cache reads cost a tenth of normal input tokens, but with big contexts even that can compound quickly. If you have ever tried to actually use the 1-million-token context Opus offers, you know how quickly the numbers can climb. RTK: Compress what your commands feed the model Agents do much more than just speak to us. They also run tools on our machines: searching through files, running tests, checking what’s installed, poking at version control, and much more. All of these tools were built for humans, long before anyone cared about tokens, so they tend to answer with long, decorated output. Consequently, they can flood our context, cost us a lot of money, and diminish the general effectiveness of the model. That’s why the RTK proxy was created. This is what the normal `docker ps` command produces. Notice the nicely rendered table that makes reading the output very easy for humans: % docker ps CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES 56e40e265f7b busybox "sleep infinity" 3 seconds ago Up 3 seconds stay-alive And this is the same command with RTK: % rtk docker ps [docker] 1 containers: 56e40e265f7b stay-alive (busybox) It is highly opinionated and can sometimes cut out information that would be useful. But thanks to those same heuristics, it saves, on average, 60% to 90% of output tokens on supported commands. Mind that this won’t translate one-to-one into AI spend: RTK tends to compact output that would usually be cached cheaply anyway. In practice, that double-digit token compression may only buy us a single-digit cost cut, but it’s still a worthy endeavor. Compress everything the agent reads and leave some Headroom Command output isn’t the only place in which we can bleed tokens. Reading code, consuming JSON, calling MCPs, sending requests, the list goes on and on. All of these can be optimized, and all of these can explode our costs if not watched. And that’s where Headroom comes in. It’s an impressively complete context optimization layer that compresses mostly everything an AI agent reads: tool outputs, logs, files, RAG chunks and even conversation history, all before it ever reaches the model. By its own numbers, it cuts 60-95% of tokens while returning the same answers. Where Caveman and RTK each target one boundary, Headroom tries to cover them all. The clever part is that it doesn’t compress everything the same way. It first works out what kind of content it’s looking at (code, logs, data, plain text) and then trims each in a way that fits. Code keeps the parts that describe what it does and drops the bulk of the bodies. Logs keep the failures and drop the passing noise. Data keeps the errors and the odd values and throws away the repetitive rest. On top of that, it’s careful not to disturb the parts of the conversation the model has already seen, so those stay cheap to reuse. The other clever part is that, unlike RTK, its compression is reversible. Instead of throwing the trimmed detail away, Headroom stashes the original locally (they call it CCR, Compress-Cache-Retrieve) and hands the model a `headroom_retrieve` tool. So when the agent actually needs the full thing, it just asks for it. Aggressive savings, without the risk of the model going blind on the one line that mattered. Mind that it can use RTK, and at the time of writing this article, it ships with it and uses it by default for shell-output rewriting. It can also employ some terseness steering, so it can also behave a little bit like Caveman. How to combine them and when to stop The good news is that these three aren’t rivals; they stack. Caveman trims what the model writes back; RTK trims what our shell hands in; and Headroom sits over the whole conversation and compresses everything else, including RTK output. A sensible starting point: let Headroom wrap our agent, keep RTK underneath it for command output, and layer Caveman on top when we want the model itself to shut up and get to the point. Each one guards a different boundary, so the savings add rather than cancel out. But compression isn’t free, and more of it isn’t always better. Every heuristic that drops a token is a small bet that the model didn’t need it. Most of the time, that bet pays off; occasionally, it hides the one log line or JSON field that mattered, and the agent guesses instead of knowing. This is exactly why Headroom’s reversible CCR is nice, but even that costs a round-trip when the model has to fetch the original back. So we should measure before we celebrate. Watch the token graphs, but also watch whether answers get worse. If our agent starts asking for things it used to just know, we’ve compressed past the sweet spot. The goal was never zero tokens; it was spending them only on buying us something. Spend Tokens Only Where They Count Agents often work in an environment that was never designed for them. It was designed for humans, in times when text wasn’t measured in tokens, and nobody had to think twice about how much a paragraph costs. They can manage, sure, but it will take time and money, and both add up faster than we’d like. At monday.com, we strive to build environments that feel natural not only to humans, but increasingly to agents too. Whether it’s teaching them to talk like a caveman, compressing their command output with RTK, or handing everything through Headroom, the underlying idea is the same: we can, and should, make their lives easier by feeding them only the content they actually need. Our agents get faster and sharper, and our context stays clean. Last but not least, we might finally stop worrying about hitting the monthly AI spend limit and truly focus on our work.

title: Alcohol and Fertility: What You Need to Know
summary: Can alcohol affect fertility? Here’s what you need to know about alcohol and fertility, including its effect on hormones, egg quality, ovulation, & conception.
body_text: Alcohol and fertility can feel confusing. One person might say, “I drank alcohol and conceived without any issues.” Another says stop drinking as soon as you start trying for a baby. So who’s right? It’s not that simple. About 12-24% of couples worldwide struggle with infertility. Alcohol is one lifestyle factor that could affect it. One study found that women who drank alcohol had a 13% lower chance of getting pregnant each cycle. Moderate-to-heavy drinking was linked to a 23% drop. (Here’s what we mean by each type of drinking : Moderate means three to six drinks a week. Heavy means more than seven. And binge drinking means four or more drinks in one day. One drink equals around 5 ounces of wine, 12 ounces of beer, or 1.5 ounces of spirits.) Keep reading to know more about the effects of alcohol and fertility, and what you can do when you’re trying to conceive. Key Takeaways The effect of alcohol on fertility largely depends on how much and how often you drink. There’s no clear “safe” amount for couples trying to conceive. Alcohol can interfere with female fertility by affecting reproductive hormones, ovulation, menstrual function, and early embryo development. Drinking moderate to large amounts of alcohol may interfere with regular menstrual cycles and increase the chances of anovulation. Light drinking is still a gray area because not all studies agree on its effects on fertility. Hormones and cycles may improve sooner after completely stopping alcohol, but recovery isn’t the same for everyone. If you’re actively trying to conceive, it’s best to avoid alcohol, especially after ovulation or if you’re undergoing fertility treatments. When it comes to conceiving, both partners’ drinking habits matter. Does alcohol affect female reproductive hormones? For your cycle to work as it should, your brain, ovaries, and uterus need to send the right signals at the right time. Alcohol can interrupt this process, but researchers are still figuring out exactly how. Moderate drinking has been linked to higher estrogen and lower progesterone. With long-term drinking, hormone levels can become harder to predict, especially if the liver is affected. Estrogen Alcohol can raise estrogen in two main ways. It can increase aromatase activity, which turns certain hormones into estrogen. It can also make it harder for the liver to break estrogen down. One study found that women who drank more alcohol had higher estradiol levels than women who drank little or none. But the difference wasn’t strong enough to prove alcohol caused the change. Another study found that drinking at least one drink a day raised estradiol levels. Women with alcohol dependence had lower levels, possibly because long-term drinking can affect the liver and hormone balance. Short-term studies found hormone changes too. In one study, about three drinks caused estrogen levels to rise within minutes . Another found that about two drinks increased testosterone and lowered androstenedione, which suggests alcohol can change how the liver processes hormones . In another study , women who drank about two drinks a day for three menstrual cycles had higher estrogen levels around ovulation and during the luteal phase. The bottom line? Alcohol may interfere with the normal hormonal balance that keeps ovulation and your menstrual cycle on track. Progesterone Progesterone helps prepare the uterus for an embryo and supports the part of your cycle after ovulation. In one study , women’s progesterone levels dropped after about two to five drinks — drinking more didn’t cause a bigger drop. Two other studies found similar results. In one, women had lower progesterone levels after taking naltrexone , a medication researchers used to study hormone control. In the other, alcohol lowered progesterone after ovulation, even when women were given hCG to boost progesterone production. Know more: How To Increase Progesterone To Get Pregnant? Does alcohol affect your egg count? There’s no test that can tell you your exact egg count or ovarian reserve. But some doctors use markers like AMH, AFC, and FSH to get a better idea. One small study found that moderate drinkers had higher FSH levels and a lower AFC than nondrinkers. That could point to lower ovarian reserve. Another study found more primordial follicles, or early egg-containing follicles, in women who drank lightly or moderately. Animal studies have raised more concern. Long-term alcohol exposure has been linked to follicle loss, follicle damage, and stress in the ovaries. Researchers can’t say that an occasional drink will age your ovaries faster. But they also can’t rule out any harm from frequent or heavy drinking. Know more: Signs of Bad Egg Quality and What You Can Do About It Does alcohol affect your menstrual cycle? Your menstrual cycle relies on hormones working together. Hormones need to rise and fall in a certain pattern. When that rhythm gets thrown off, you could notice longer or shorter cycles, bleeding between periods, or missed periods. Studies in women with alcohol abuse found: More irregular menstrual cycles Greater variability in cycle length Shorter bleeding More bleeding between periods Some studies found similar FSH and LH levels in drinkers and nondrinkers. This could mean liver problems from long-term drinking play a bigger role than just alcohol. Can alcohol make period symptoms worse? Alcohol causes dehydration and can mess with your sleep. It can also make headaches, bloating, tiredness, and mood changes feel worse. Research has linked frequent drinking to longer-lasting period pain , PMS, heavy bleeding, and other menstrual problems. Binge drinking has also been tied to more symptoms. Say you have drinks with friends on Friday night, then your period starts Saturday morning. Now you’re dealing with cramps, poor sleep, a headache, and dehydration all at once. Can alcohol interfere with ovulation? Possibly yes. Ovulation happens when an ovary releases a mature egg. If that egg isn’t released, you can’t conceive naturally during that cycle. One three-week study found cycle problems in about half of the social drinkers and 60% of the heavier drinkers. The most common issue was anovulation, which means no egg was released. It was also linked to lower LH levels. Another study found that about three to four drinks didn’t change LH release after stimulation. This could mean alcohol affects an earlier part of the process, possibly in the hypothalamus. The biggest concerns come from regular, moderate-to-heavy, or binge drinking. There isn’t enough evidence to know how light or occasional drinking affects ovulation. Can alcohol affect your chances of pregnancy? Getting pregnant takes more than releasing an egg. Several steps have to happen at the right time. One study found that moderate-to-heavy drinking during the luteal phase, which starts after ovulation, could disrupt the hormonal changes needed for conception. The research on light drinking isn’t as clear. But there’s no official “safe” amount of alcohol. Natural conception Some studies have linked alcohol to a lower chance of pregnancy. Women who drank more than seven drinks a week often took longer to conceive. Other research found that higher alcohol intake was tied to a lower chance of getting pregnant each cycle. Still, the results aren’t all the same. One study found that wine drinkers were slightly less likely to take more than 12 months to conceive than nondrinkers or people who drank beer or spirits. That doesn’t mean wine helps fertility. It just shows that the research is mixed. Assisted reproductive treatments (ART) Fertility treatments can involve a lot of uncertainty, waiting, and plenty of stress. Studies have linked drinking during fertility treatment to: Fewer eggs retrieved Reduced embryo quality Poorer embryo development Fewer embryos reaching the stage needed for implantation Lower pregnancy rates One study found that women who had more than seven drinks a week were 7% less likely to get pregnant after fertility treatment than women who didn’t drink. Their chance of a live birth also dropped by 9% when their male partners drank the same amount. Know more: IVF Success Rates: The Factors That Affect Your Chances Does alcohol affect implantation? After fertilization, the embryo still needs to grow, reach the uterus, and attach to the uterine lining. There aren’t many studies on alcohol and implantation. But lab studies suggest alcohol could affect early embryo growth and the cells that help implantation happen. Is alcohol linked to ectopic pregnancy? Some lab studies suggest alcohol could affect the muscle contractions that help move an embryo through the fallopian tube. But researchers haven’t confirmed that this raises the risk of an ectopic pregnancy. Can drinking alcohol while pregnant hurt the baby? Yes — this is where the link is clear. There’s no known safe amount of alcohol during pregnancy. Drinking during pregnancy has been linked to: Miscarriage Stillbirth Premature birth Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASDs) Sudden infant death syndrome, or SIDS Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders ( FASDs ) can lead to lifelong problems with learning, behavior, thinking, and physical health. FASDs can range from mild to severe. They’re also preventable by not drinking during pregnancy. If you drank before getting a positive test, don’t panic. Stop drinking and talk with your healthcare provider for support and next steps. When should I quit if I’m planning to start TTC? The best time to stop drinking is before you start trying to conceive, or TTC. This gives your body more time to recover and support healthy reproductive function. Recovery looks different for everyone. It depends on how much you drink, how long you’ve been drinking, and your overall health. Stopping before your first unprotected cycle also avoids alcohol exposure during ovulation, fertilization, implantation, and early pregnancy. If your male partner drinks , stopping about three months before trying gives new sperm time to develop. There’s no magic reset date. But the earlier you stop, the more time your body has to adjust. How much alcohol is safe while trying to conceive? There’s no known safe amount of alcohol while trying to conceive. Pregnancy can begin before you know it’s happened. Alcohol can also affect a pregnancy soon after implantation. That’s why major health organizations recommend avoiding alcohol once you start trying, especially after ovulation or during fertility treatment. Skipping alcohol won’t guarantee pregnancy. But there’s also no amount that’s been shown to improve your chances. If you drink and later find out you’re pregnant, stop drinking and talk with your doctor if you’re concerned. Know more: Can Alcohol Affect A Pregnancy Test? How can you stop drinking when TTC? This can feel harder than it sounds, especially if drinking is part of your routine. A little planning can make it easier: Pick a clear stop date. Remove alcohol from your home. Keep alcohol-free drinks nearby. Ask your partner, family, or friends for support. Notice your triggers. Do you drink when you’re stressed, bored, tired, or out with friends? Replace the habit with something else, like a walk, tea, a mocktail, or reading. Ask your partner to join — it feels less lonely when one person isn’t drinking while the other is tracking ovulation and taking prenatal vitamins. If cutting back feels difficult, talk with your doctor or an addiction specialist. You deserve support, not judgment. So, what’s the link between alcohol and fertility? Alcohol and fertility are connected, but the effect isn’t the same for everyone. Frequent or heavy drinking can affect hormones, ovulation, periods, implantation, and early pregnancy. The research on light drinking is less clear. There’s no known safe amount of alcohol while trying to conceive or during pregnancy. Experts recommend stopping once you start trying for a baby. It won’t guarantee pregnancy. But it’s one simple step that can support your fertility and a healthier pregnancy. FAQs Does alcohol affect fertility? It can. Heavy, frequent, or binge drinking can affect hormones, ovulation, sperm health, and your chances of conceiving. Does drinking alcohol affect your fertility? Yes, especially at higher amounts. The research on light or occasional drinking is less clear. How long after quitting drinking does fertility come back? There’s no set timeline. It can take weeks or months, depending on how much you drank, how long you drank, and your overall health. What is the 1/2/3 rule for drinking? It usually means one drink per hour, two per occasion, and three alcohol-free days a week. But it isn’t a fertility guideline. How long should you stop drinking before trying to conceive? It’s best to stop drinking before you begin trying to conceive. Men could consider stopping about three months before TTC to give new sperm time to develop. Does quitting alcohol improve egg quality? Quitting won’t reverse age-related changes or guarantee better eggs. But it can support healthier hormones, sleep, nutrition, and overall reproductive health. How long does it take for sperm to recover after drinking? A new sperm cycle takes about 74 days. Changes are often seen after three months, but recovery can take longer after heavy or long-term drinking. Can a man drink alcohol when trying to conceive? He can, but heavy drinking can affect hormones and sperm health. Cutting back or stopping about three months before conception can help support healthier sperm. Does alcohol lower male fertility? Heavy drinking can lower male fertility by affecting hormones, sexual health, sperm count, and sperm quality. The effect of light or moderate drinking is less clear. How long after quitting alcohol will sperm improve? It can take about three months for healthier changes to show up in new sperm. The timeline depends on past drinking habits and overall health. Should you stop drinking completely when trying to conceive? That’s the safest choice. Pregnancy can begin before a test turns positive, and avoiding alcohol removes one possible risk during conception and early pregnancy.
